title: Elul: getting ready
hookLine: the shofar sounds on Elul mornings, and prayers for forgiveness begin
last: THE KING IS IN THE FIELD.

cards: A weekday morning in late summer. The service is ending, people are folding their prayer shawls, someone is already checking their phone. Then, from the front, a sound cuts through everything: a ram's horn.
A long, raw blast, then broken notes, then a long one again. It isn't a holiday. It's an ordinary Tuesday in Elul, and in many synagogues this happens every weekday morning for a month.

teach.b: In Ashkenazi communities, the shofar is blown after the morning service through most of Elul, though not on Shabbat and not on the day before Rosh Hashanah. A wake-up call, a month early.
The great medieval teacher Maimonides wrote that the shofar seems to say: sleepers, wake up from your sleep; look at your deeds and return.
Then come the selichot, the prayers for forgiveness. Selichah means pardon. Sephardi communities rise early and say them through the whole month of Elul.
Ashkenazi communities begin later, usually on the Saturday night before Rosh Hashanah, sometimes around midnight, and continue until Yom Kippur.
Either way, the heart of every selichot service is the same: the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
They come from the moment after the golden calf, when God passes before Moses and proclaims: "The LORD, the LORD, God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth."
The Talmud, in Rosh Hashanah 17b, pictures God wrapped in a prayer shawl like a prayer leader, showing Moses this order of prayer and promising that whenever Israel recites it, they will be answered.
So the selichot repeat it again and again. Why a whole month?

Tradition says Moses went back up the mountain for a second set of tablets at the start of Elul, and came down forty days later, on what became Yom Kippur. Elul is the runway: you don't arrive at the Days of Awe cold.

how: In Ashkenazi synagogues the shofar is blown after weekday morning prayers during Elul, and selichot begin the Saturday night before Rosh Hashanah; Sephardi communities recite selichot early each morning throughout Elul.

games.q: you're a synagogue in Elul. Shabbat morning arrives. do you blow the shofar after the service?
o: yes, every single day of Elul.
no: not on Shabbat, and not on the day before Rosh Hashanah.
games.why: the Elul shofar skips Shabbat and the day before Rosh Hashanah, so the new year's own blasts stand apart.

practice: If you can, play a recording of a shofar, or let the bell at the start of this sit be your wake-up call. When the sound fades, ask one honest question, what from this past year needs looking at, and let it stand without solving it.
If you pray, you can say the line from Exodus: merciful and gracious.

wordCard.voice: Selichot. Prayers for pardon, built around the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, said in the weeks before Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

carryVoice: Your line: thirty days to get ready. Sleepers, wake up, and look at your deeds. See you tomorrow.
